items.title: Topic Ten Opens: Craving and Aversion, and the Six Feelings That Grow From Them

items.zh: 貪恚何因緣？由何故欣、慼、毛竪、意尋思，如孩依乳母？
items.en: What is the cause of craving and aversion? What gives rise to delight and sorrow, to hair standing on end, and to mental rumination — clinging as a child clings to its wet-nurse?

items.zh: 潤所生、自生，如諾瞿陀樹；別縛於諸欲，猶摩迦處林。是貪恚因緣，由斯故欣、慼、毛竪、意尋思，如孩依乳母。知彼彼因緣，生已尋除滅；超昔未超海，暴流無後有。
items.en: Born of moisture, and born of themselves — like the banyan tree. Bound each to its own desire, as the vine binds the forest. These are the causes of craving and aversion, and from them come delight and sorrow, hair standing on end, and mental rumination — as a child clings to its wet-nurse. Knowing each cause as it truly is, the moment it arises one at once extinguishes it. What was never crossed before is crossed at last — the flood, never to return.

items.zh: 今此頌中，云何貪恚？謂如有一，處在居家，於可意境、可意有情共相會遇，而生貪著；於不可意境及有情共相會遇，而生瞋恚。云何欣慼？謂如有一，於佛所證法毘奈耶，率爾得生須臾正信，不善觀察前後得失，忽然自勵，便棄家法，往趣非家。既出家已，與凡道俗共相雜住；遂於去來貨財親友追念思慕，憂慼纏心。或復有一，非由正信，亦非自勵，往趣非家。然或為王之所驅迫，乃至或為不活邪畏之所恐怖，捨離居家。既出家已，於其正信諸婆羅門、居士等邊，時時多獲利養恭敬，深生愛味。竊作念言：吾此一方善哉奇要，無勞稼穡，不事商賈，少致艱辛，足堪活命。彼緣如是利養恭敬，便自欣悅安然而住。云何毛竪及意尋思？謂如有一，非由自勵，不為活命，捨離居家；然由正信，捐棄家法，往趣非家。既出家已，不與道俗共相雜住，便臻遠離，寂靜閑居。彼閑居時，或於塵霧，或昏夜分，見大雲氣，聞震雷音；或逢雹雨師子虎豹；或遭凶猾竊劫抄虜；或遇非人來相嬈逼；便生驚怖，身毛為竪。或至晝分，於彼去來妙欲親友，發依耽嗜所有尋思。謂欲尋思，如經廣說，乃至家世相應尋思。如是已說貪恚等事。云何潤生及與自生，猶如世間諾瞿陀樹？潤名愛水。由此為緣，能生諸取。彼貪恚等，一切皆用此為共緣。自者，即是貪恚為先，尋思為後，各各差別種子界性。云何貪恚乃至尋思別縛諸欲，猶如世間摩魯迦條纏繞林樹？謂略說有六種別欲。或有身手力所引致現在事欲，謂居家者所有諸欲。於此境界，用此為緣，發生貪恚。或有從他所得種種現在事欲，謂為活命而出家者所有諸欲。於此境界，用此為緣，發生欣悅。或有過去、未來事欲，謂忽自勵而出家者所有諸欲。於此境界，用此為緣，發生憂慼。或有所餘諸煩惱欲，略有二種。謂於欲界自體及資身命。或有未斷妄分別貪，謂由正信而出家者，寂靜閑居，於塵夜分所遭眾事。於此境界，用此為緣，便生驚怖，身毛為竪。或有未斷妄分別貪，所謂即此補特伽羅至晝日分，於外色聲香味觸境，用此為緣，發生意地所有尋思。又有沙門、若婆羅門，如實了知如前所說貪與恚等及彼因緣，又能了知眾緣生法無常性已，隨其所生不起貪著，即便棄捨、變吐、斷滅。離色、無色二界貪故，度有暴流；離欲貪故，度欲暴流。如是暴流昔所未度，今既度已，終無有退。復次，今當略辨上所說義。謂薄伽梵於此頌中，略顯三位。一、在家位，二、出家位，三、遠離位。又略顯示共與不共因緣所生若愛、若恚，於諸欲中二種別縛，及斷方便，并斷勝利。當知是名此中略義。又於此中，若貪、若欣、若依耽嗜所有尋思，當知愛品；若恚、若慼及與驚怖，當知恚品。

blocks.text: A short verse dialogue, then a long explanation, **almost all untranslated** (0376c19–0377b15). It is one of the most psychologically detailed passages in this part of the treatise.

What is the cause of craving and aversion, of delight and sorrow, of hair standing on end, of rumination, clinging "as a child clings to its wet-nurse"? Master Cháng Bǎi: the six afflictions are the child; the conditions they rely on are the nurse. The answer: they are "born of moisture and born of themselves, like the banyan tree; bound each to its own desire, as a vine binds the forest."
The prose describes three stages of life, each with its own afflictions:

items: **At home.** Meeting pleasant things and people, one craves; meeting unpleasant ones, one is averse.

**Gone forth.** Someone who goes forth on a sudden burst of faith, without considering carefully, and then lives among worldly people, comes to miss past wealth and friends: **sorrow**. Someone who goes forth not from faith but under pressure, from a king or from fear of poverty, and then receives generous offerings, thinks, "What a good arrangement! No ploughing, no trading, little hardship." That is **delight**.

**In solitude.** Someone who goes forth from real faith and lives alone in the forest may be frightened at night by thunder, hail, wild animals, robbers, or spirits: **hair standing on end**. By day, thoughts of past pleasures and friends arise: **rumination**.

blocks.text: "**Moisture**" is the water of craving: the common condition of all six. "**Born of themselves**" refers to each affliction's own seed: the individual condition. Master Cháng Bǎi: the banyan's hanging branches root and grow into new trees, as afflictions grow from one another.

"**Bound each to its own desire**" means six kinds of desire, each binding as a vine binds a tree: present objects gained by one's own effort (the householder, giving craving and aversion); objects received from others (the one who went forth for a living, giving delight); past and future objects (the one who went forth on impulse, giving sorrow); and the afflictions themselves and the unabandoned false conceptions (giving fear and rumination).

Ascetics who know these afflictions and their causes, and see that conditioned things are impermanent, let them go as they arise, and so cross the floods of desire and existence, never to fall back. Master Cháng Bǎi: 尋 here means "immediately".
The prose groups greed, delight, and rumination with **craving**; aversion, sorrow, and fear with **aversion**.

quiz.q: What does the deity ask in the tenth topic, and with what image?
options: the causes of craving, aversion, delight, sorrow, hair standing on end, and rumination — like a child clinging to its wet-nurse
quiz.why: The question verse: what is the cause of craving and aversion? What gives rise to delight and sorrow, to hair standing on end, and to mental rumination — clinging as a child clings to its wet-nurse?

quiz.q: In "like a child clinging to its wet-nurse," what do the child and the nurse stand for, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the child is the six afflictions; the nurse is the conditions they depend on
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the child stands for the six mental afflictions — craving, aversion, delight, sorrow, hair standing on end, and rumination; the conditions they rely on are the wet-nurse.

quiz.q: "Born of moisture, and born of themselves — like the banyan tree." How do the masters describe the banyan?
options: Cháng Bǎi: a huge tree whose branches touch the ground and grow into new trees; Miào Jìng: it stands for craving, an obstacle to the path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the banyan is a knotless tree with a round, massive trunk; its branches hang to the ground and grow into another banyan. Venerable Miào Jìng: it really means craving — this attachment is a condition obstructing the path.

quiz.q: "生已尋除滅" is rendered "one seeks it out the moment it arises." How does Master Cháng Bǎi read 尋?
options: "immediately" — the moment affliction arises it is eliminated; the English reads it as "seek"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having known the causes of affliction, the moment affliction arises one immediately eliminates it. 尋 means "immediately"; the English "seeks it out" reads it as "search."

quiz.q: In "born of moisture, born of themselves," what does Master Cháng Bǎi say are the common and the individual causes of affliction?
options: the common cause is craving; the individual cause is each one's own seed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the common condition of affliction is craving; the individual condition is each one's own seed — from these, affliction arises. Venerable Miào Jìng: every dharma has its own seed; the seed as cause is "born of themselves."
